question: Why should community health nurses team up with traditional birth attendants and local leaders?

options.A: To collect financial taxes from rural households
options.B: To stop all traditional practices permanently by force
options.C: To ensure coordinated care and prompt referral of dangerous cases
options.D: To hand over all clinical nursing duties to local leaders

explanation: Working hand-in-hand with local leaders builds strong community trust, ensuring that mothers with complications get rushed to the hospital safely and quickly. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T14#GNS324_U3_T14_h8)

question: Why might a nurse mistakenly refuse or delay PAC care due to legal fears?

options.A: Absence of any regulatory guidelines from the Nursing Council
options.B: Confusion between performing an abortion and treating its emergency complications
options.C: Strict hospital policies requiring police clearance for all emergency admissions
options.D: Lack of basic nursing equipment in rural health clinics

explanation: Some providers get scared, mistakenly thinking that treating post-abortion complications makes them an accomplice to an illegal act. Remember: treating complications is saving a life! [learn more](GNS226_U5_T024#GNS226_U5_T024_h4)

question: A pregnant woman in your community presents with a rigid, painful tummy and dark bleeding. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Ectopic pregnancy
options.B: Urinary tract infection
options.C: Placental abruption
options.D: Normal bloody show

explanation: You nailed it! When the placenta separates early, blood gets trapped behind it, causing a painful, hard uterus and dark bleeding. Keep up the brilliant thinking! [learn more](GNS225_U3_T13#GNS225_U3_T13_h2)

question: Why is delayed bathing recommended for stable newborns immediately after birth?

options.A: It allows the umbilical cord stump to dry
options.B: It helps preserve vernix for skin immunity
options.C: It prevents early neonatal jaundice spikes
options.D: It prevents rapid heat loss and cold stress

explanation: Washing a wet baby too soon strips away heat through evaporation, putting them at high risk for dangerous drops in body temperature. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T51#GNS214_U1_T51_h4)

question: Why is it smart not to throw away the broth after boiling vegetables?

options.A: It slows down digestion so much that hunger never returns
options.B: It neutralizes all harmful bacteria that may have survived the cooking process
options.C: It recaptures water-soluble vitamins and minerals that leaked out during boiling
options.D: It provides all the dietary protein required for the day in one serving

explanation: Brilliant! Drinking the soup broth ensures you don't lose all those valuable vitamins that leaked out into the water. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T009#GNS227_U4_T009_h5)

question: What is the main goal of a Clinical Decision Support System (CDSS)?

options.A: To monitor hospital room temperatures and environmental safety
options.B: To provide targeted recommendations and safety alerts based on client data
options.C: To schedule client appointments and manage billing operations
options.D: To automatically diagnose complex diseases without physician input

explanation: A CDSS is like a smart assistant on the computer that gives helpful pop-ups, like drug allergy warnings, to keep your patient safe. [learn more](GNS113_U3_T4#GNS113_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the main purpose of the Incident Command System during a disaster?

options.A: To place financial responsibility solely on local nursing staff
options.B: To establish a clear chain of command and organized coordination
options.C: To allow every responder to make independent medical decisions
options.D: To eliminate the need for medical triage protocols

explanation: Well done! This system keeps everyone organized with clear leadership roles, stopping chaos and confusion when multiple agencies respond. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T3#GNS315_U1_T3_h5)

question: What is the main benefit of conducting formative research before launching a community health campaign?

options.A: It proves that foreign health theories are always superior
options.B: It helps nurses understand local beliefs and design appropriate messages
options.C: It eliminates the need to speak the local language
options.D: It guarantees that the government will release extra funds

explanation: Formative research simply means doing your homework on the community first. It helps you design messages that truly fit the people you want to help. You're going to make a brilliant community health nurse! [learn more](GNS124_U5_T8#GNS124_U5_T8_h5)

question: Which of these is NOT something you should do when scaling up a quality improvement project?

options.A: Providing ongoing education for all affected personnel
options.B: Continuously monitoring performance metrics over time
options.C: Appointing champions or leaders on each new unit
options.D: Firing all staff members who question the new change

explanation: That's definitely not it! Firing people who ask questions destroys team spirit. Scaling up successfully takes teaching, support, and patience—never punishment. [learn more](GST319_U3_T4#GST319_U3_T4_h6)

question: According to the Nigerian immunization schedule, which vaccine is given to a newborn baby right at birth?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid booster
options.B: Yellow fever vaccine
options.C: Measles vaccine
options.D: BCG vaccine

explanation: Correct! BCG protects babies against tuberculosis and is given right away at birth alongside the polio drops. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T12#GNS313_U2_T12_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT an effective strategy for preventing the spread of gastroenteritis in a community?

options.A: Giving rotavirus vaccines to young infants
options.B: Using over-the-counter antidiarrheal drugs daily
options.C: Washing hands regularly with soap and clean water
options.D: Ensuring access to safe and treated drinking water

explanation: Daily antidiarrheal drugs do not prevent infections or transmission; hygiene, safe water, and vaccination are the true preventive measures. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T20#GNS313_U2_T20_h6)

question: Which type of dietary fiber is best known for adding bulk to stool and keeping things moving smoothly in the gut?

options.A: Simple fiber
options.B: Glycogen fiber
options.C: Soluble fiber
options.D: Insoluble fiber

explanation: Spot on! Insoluble fiber doesn't break down easily, so it adds bulk and helps prevent constipation. [learn more](GNS227_U1_T008#GNS227_U1_T008_h5)

question: What responsibility do nurses hold regarding data integrity in the electronic health record?

options.A: Ensuring accurate and timely data entry to protect patient safety
options.B: Writing the underlying computer code for the hospital software
options.C: Repairing broken hardware terminals in patient rooms
options.D: Setting up new user accounts for incoming hospital doctors

explanation: Nurses must enter correct information carefully because mistakes in the chart can directly harm patient care. [learn more](GNS113_U2_T4#GNS113_U2_T4_h6)

question: Which medication is an opioid antagonist that blocks the effects of alcohol and opioids?

options.A: Naltrexone
options.B: Buprenorphine
options.C: Methadone
options.D: Lorazepam

explanation: Naltrexone binds to and blocks opioid receptors, preventing alcohol and opioids from activating the brain's reward pathways. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T12#GNS125_U2_T12_h7)

question: What happens to staff morale if hospital management uses MBO goals purely as a punitive tool?

options.A: Nurses become significantly more motivated to achieve higher targets
options.B: Patient satisfaction scores rise immediately due to strict rules
options.C: Administrative efficiency increases across all hospital departments
options.D: Staff feel anxious and view the process with fear rather than trust

explanation: Using goals to punish creates a toxic culture where staff hide mistakes instead of collaborating to fix them. [learn more](GST321_U2_T5#GST321_U2_T5_h6)

question: Why is it important to regularly check the connection joints of an IV setup?

options.A: To ensure the gravity roller clamp is set to the maximum speed
options.B: To check if the plastic tubing needs to be warmed with a heating pad
options.C: To make sure the manufacturer label matches the client's chart
options.D: To prevent accidental disconnection, fluid leakage, and bacterial entry

explanation: Keeping connections tight keeps the system sterile! It stops messy leaks and prevents nasty bacteria from sneaking into your patient's bloodstream. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T17#GNS122_U1_T17_h5)

question: What is the main cause of communicable (spreadable) diseases?

options.A: Genetically inherited cellular mutations
options.B: Nutritional deficiencies in the diet
options.C: Long-term exposure to industrial chemicals
options.D: Infectious agents like bacteria and viruses

explanation: You nailed it! Communicable diseases are caused by tiny living germs like bacteria and viruses that can pass from one person to another. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T13#GNS313_U1_T13_h1)

question: A pregnant patient asks if she can safely drink fresh, unpasteurized goat milk. What is your best response as a nurse?

options.A: Yes, as long as the goat appears healthy and clean
options.B: No, because raw milk may contain dangerous Listeria or Brucella
options.C: No, but only because raw milk causes severe lactose intolerance
options.D: Yes, because goat milk naturally lacks all human pathogens

explanation: You're doing great! Pregnant women should always avoid raw milk because it can harbor nasty infections like Listeria and Brucella that harm both mother and baby. [learn more](GST114_U3_T4#GST114_U3_T4_h3)

question: A patient with severe bleeding after childbirth is in shock, but blood isn't ready at the bank yet. What should you do first?

options.A: Mobilize family donors for replacement and start rapid IV crystalloids while waiting
options.B: Wait patiently until the blood bank completes routine screening hours later
options.C: Administer strong vasopressors without starting any fluid replacement
options.D: Discharge the patient home with oral iron supplements

explanation: Great nursing judgment! In real clinical practice, we start IV fluids right away and quickly rally family members to donate blood while we wait. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h8)

question: Which of these is a great example of primary prevention in the home?

options.A: Performing range-of-motion exercises for a stroke survivor
options.B: Checking blood sugar levels to find early diabetes
options.C: Giving a seasonal flu vaccine to a healthy client
options.D: Treating an open pressure ulcer on the heel

explanation: Primary prevention stops illnesses before they even start. Giving a vaccine to a healthy person is a classic way to protect them! [learn more](GNS324_U3_T9#GNS324_U3_T9_h2)

question: Which of these methods is NOT reliable for destroying infectious prions?

options.A: Using disposable instruments
options.B: Extended chemical disinfection
options.C: Standard boiling in water
options.D: Specialized high-heat autoclaving

explanation: Spot on! Prions are super tough and survive normal boiling. They need heavy-duty, specialized sterilization protocols to be destroyed. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T5#GNS222_U4_T5_h7)

question: Which Nigerian law specifically tackles harmful traditional practices and gender-based violence?

options.A: National Health Insurance Authority Act
options.B: Violence Against Persons Prohibition (VAPP) Act
options.C: Criminal Code for Corporate Fraud
options.D: Standard Environmental Sanitation Decree

explanation: The VAPP Act gives law enforcement a legal tool to protect people from physical, emotional, and traditional abuse, including harmful widowhood practices. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T10#GNS225_U6_T10_h4)

question: A patient arrives with a massive pulmonary embolism. What is happening in their body?

options.A: Blood flow through the pulmonary arteries is blocked, impairing oxygenation
options.B: The liver has stopped producing clotting factors, causing widespread bleeding
options.C: An infection in the urinary tract has spread into the spinal fluid
options.D: Gastric acid is leaking directly into the peritoneal cavity through an ulcer

explanation: A pulmonary embolism is a blocked blood vessel in the lungs. Because the blockage is there, blood can't pick up fresh oxygen to circulate. [learn more](GNS315_U2_T4#GNS315_U2_T4_h3)

question: How do poor food supply systems directly impact clinical nursing practice?

options.A: By forcing nurses to work directly as agricultural extension officers
options.B: By completely eliminating the need for hospital admission records
options.C: By reducing the total number of patients seeking emergency care
options.D: By increasing cases of malnutrition and diet-related illnesses

explanation: Inadequate food systems lead directly to health conditions like malnutrition and chronic diseases that nurses treat in clinical settings. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h1)

question: A patient with a deep, dirty wound hasn't had a tetanus shot in 10 years. The doctor orders a tetanus vaccine AND tetanus immune globulin. Why give the immune globulin?

options.A: To stimulate the patient's innate physical barriers in the skin and mucous membranes
options.B: To cure any chronic autoimmune disease the patient might already have
options.C: To provide immediate, short-term protection against toxins while the vaccine takes effect
options.D: To permanently replace the patient's bone marrow cells with donor tissue

explanation: The immune globulin gives instant borrowed antibodies to fight fast-acting toxins right now, while waiting for the actual vaccine to stimulate the patient's own body to make long-term defense. [learn more](GST114_U4_T6#GST114_U4_T6_h5)

question: What is a major role of Community Health Workers in maternal and child health?

options.A: Replacing professional nurses entirely in district hospitals
options.B: Conducting household visits and referring clients with danger signs to clinics
options.C: Importing foreign medical equipment for government clinics
options.D: Performing complex major surgeries in rural health posts

explanation: You got it! Community health workers bridge the gap by visiting homes, sharing health tips, and sending anyone with danger signs straight to the clinic. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T43#GNS214_U1_T43_h8)

question: When you digest carbohydrates, what is the main sugar that enters your bloodstream?

options.A: Glucose
options.B: Glucagon
options.C: Glycerol
options.D: Glycogen

explanation: Glucose is the star player here! It is the primary, easy-to-use sugar that our bodies and brains love to burn for quick energy. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T8#GNS121_U1_T8_h3)

question: Why do doctors order genetic tests like FISH or karyotyping for blood cancers?

options.A: To find the patient's blood group for a transfusion
options.B: To find specific chromosome changes and gene mutations
options.C: To measure how much blood was lost in surgery
options.D: To see how fast red blood cells settle in a tube

explanation: Looking at the genetic makeup of the cancer cells helps the medical team figure out the best treatment plan for the patient. [learn more](GNS311_U2_T5#GNS311_U2_T5_h6)

question: During labor, a first-time mother with a history of Type III FGM is at the highest risk for which complication?

options.A: Complete absence of uterine contractions
options.B: Rapid precipitous delivery within ten minutes
options.C: Obstructed labor due to rigid scar tissue
options.D: Immediate postpartum hemorrhage from the placenta

explanation: The tough scar tissue from infibulation makes it hard for the birth canal to stretch naturally, frequently leading to obstructed labor. [learn more](GNS312_U1_T3#GNS312_U1_T3_h6)

question: What kind of pupil change do you expect to see in a patient with organophosphate poisoning (cholinergic toxidrome)?

options.A: Pinpoint pupils
options.B: Unreactive fixed pupils
options.C: Widely dilated pupils
options.D: Unequal pupil sizes

explanation: Organophosphates overstimulate the nervous system, which famously causes the pupils to shrink down to tiny, pinpoint sizes (miosis). [learn more](GNS215_U5_T5#GNS215_U5_T5_h3)

question: A patient with stable blood pressure comes to a clinic after losing their home in a disaster, and their blood pressure is suddenly very high. Why?

options.A: An intentional overdose of emergency relief food
options.B: Exposure to cold weather causing elevated heart rates
options.C: Disruption of routine medication access and extreme environmental stress
options.D: Sudden permanent cure of their baseline hypertension

explanation: Spot on! Disasters cut off regular medications and create heavy stress, which easily triggers spikes in conditions like high blood pressure. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h3)

question: Think of a research study design as a map or plan. What is its main job?

options.A: To act as a blueprint for answering a clinical question
options.B: To write the final conclusion of the research paper
options.C: To calculate the total budget needed for the project
options.D: To recruit patients for clinical drug trials

explanation: Great job! Just like building a house needs a drawing, a study design is your step-by-step plan for gathering and checking your information. [learn more](GNS217_U3_T13#GNS217_U3_T13_h1)

question: How does menu planning directly impact the budget of a food service unit?

options.A: It has no impact whatsoever on the overall kitchen expenses
options.B: It automatically sets the electricity tariff for the entire hospital building
options.C: It dictates the monthly salary of all administrative personnel
options.D: It determines the types of ingredients purchased and the amount of waste generated

explanation: The menu dictates your shopping list, which directly controls how much money you spend and waste. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T005#GNS227_U3_T005_h6)

question: What is the main rule for deciding what counts toward a country's Gross National Product (GNP)?

options.A: Approval by the World Health Organization
options.B: Physical location inside the national borders
options.C: Tax exemption status of the business
options.D: Citizenship or ownership by permanent residents

explanation: While GDP looks at geography, GNP focuses on who owns the production or who performs the work based on citizenship. [learn more](GST322_U3_T1#GST322_U3_T1_h3)

question: What is the primary focus of microbiology in nursing practice?

options.A: Synthesizing new pharmaceutical drugs in the ward
options.B: Calculating precise fluid balance for dehydrated patients
options.C: Understanding microscopic organisms and how they spread
options.D: Operating advanced diagnostic laboratory machinery

explanation: Microbiology studies tiny organisms like bacteria and viruses so nurses can understand how they cause disease and how to stop them. [learn more](GST114_U1_T3#GST114_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why do care staff encourage residents to do parts of their morning routine all by themselves?

options.A: To reduce the total number of staff members needed on duty
options.B: To eliminate the need for any individualized service plans
options.C: To comply with federal acute care hospital regulations
options.D: To prevent physical decline caused by lack of use

explanation: Great thinking! Letting residents do what they can manage preserves their muscle strength, coordination, and sense of pride. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T6#GNS324_U5_T6_h3)

question: What happens to most of the developing follicles in the ovary during a typical cycle?

options.A: They turn directly into the corpus luteum
options.B: They migrate into the fallopian tubes
options.C: They all release eggs simultaneously
options.D: They degenerate through atresia

explanation: Even though a group of follicles starts growing each month, only one becomes the champion (dominant) follicle. The rest quietly break down through a natural process called atresia. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T7#GNS121_U5_T7_h2)

question: Why do nurse researchers usually study a smaller sample instead of tracking every single patient in the country?

options.A: It ensures that zero ethical approvals are required from the hospital
options.B: It guarantees that every single patient receives direct medical treatment
options.C: It completely eliminates all forms of human error in data collection
options.D: It saves time, money, and resources while still providing useful data

explanation: Spot on! Trying to study an entire population is almost always impossible. Taking a smaller, well-chosen sample makes your research practical and achievable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T17#GNS224_U1_T17_h1)

question: Which of these is a key feature of teacher-centred teaching methods?

options.A: The classroom has no formal structure or predefined schedule
options.B: The teacher observes quietly while students teach each other
options.C: The students spend all class time performing independent research
options.D: The educator acts as the primary information giver while learners listen

explanation: In a teacher-centred setup (like a classic lecture), the instructor does most of the talking and passes information directly to the listening students. [learn more](GST321_U8_T6#GST321_U8_T6_h2)

question: Which white blood cells are our most abundant and fast-acting fighters against bacteria?

options.A: Neutrophils
options.B: Basophils
options.C: Memory cells
options.D: Eosinophils

explanation: Well done! Neutrophils are usually the very first white blood cells to rush to the scene of a fresh bacterial infection. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h3)

question: When is a retrospective nursing audit done?

options.A: After the patient has been discharged from the hospital
options.B: While the patient is actively receiving treatment on the ward
options.C: Before the patient is even admitted to the emergency room
options.D: During the exact moment a surgical operation is happening

explanation: You got it! Think of 'retrospective' as looking backward—these audits review completed medical records after the patient has already left the facility. [learn more](GST319_U4_T3#GST319_U4_T3_h3)

question: A nurse is helping design a public health program to tackle malnutrition in local primary schools. Which type of dietitian should lead this?

options.A: Clinical dietitian
options.B: Renal dietitian
options.C: Surgical dietitian
options.D: Community dietitian

explanation: Community dietitians focus on public health, schools, and larger group or population-wide nutrition programs. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T001#GNS227_U4_T001_h4)

question: What important advice should a nurse give a patient using the misoprostol-only method?

options.A: It has a 100 percent success rate on the first try
options.B: It requires staying in the hospital for three days
options.C: It has a higher rate of incomplete abortion than combination regimens
options.D: It never causes any physical discomfort

explanation: Being honest helps patients know that a follow-up visit might be needed since misoprostol alone isn't quite as strong as combination drugs. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T013#GNS226_U5_T013_h5)

question: Which of the following is NOT a normal function or feature of the large intestine?

options.A: Housing beneficial bacteria that synthesize vitamin K
options.B: Secreting primary enzymes to digest complex proteins
options.C: Storing waste material temporarily in the rectum
options.D: Reabsorbing water to form solid feces

explanation: Protein digestion happens in the stomach and small intestine; the large intestine does not secrete digestive enzymes for proteins. [learn more](GNS121_U1_T6#GNS121_U1_T6_h7)

question: A public health nurse writes a summary stating that teenage mothers in a rural ward have high rates of anemia due to poor nutrition and lack of antenatal care. What is this process called?

options.A: Hospital triage
options.B: Medical prescription
options.C: Community diagnosis
options.D: Surgical audit

explanation: Synthesizing data to identify health deficits, vulnerable groups, and causes in a population is known as a community diagnosis. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h4)

question: A community has strong local leadership and plenty of food supplies even though droughts happen often. What do we call these strengths?

options.A: A structural mitigation measure
options.B: An indicator of high vulnerability
options.C: A primary environmental hazard
options.D: A community capacity resource

explanation: Well done! Capacities are simply the strengths and resources a community uses to stand strong against disasters. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T11#GNS315_U5_T11_h2)

question: Which situation means a child needs intravenous (IV) fluids right away?

options.A: Low-grade fever lasting less than an hour
options.B: A slight decrease in daily appetite
options.C: Mild loose stool passed twice in one day
options.D: Severe dehydration with signs of shock

explanation: When shock and severe dehydration set in, drinking isn't enough anymore. IV fluids are urgently needed to restore blood pressure and save the day. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T56#GNS214_U1_T56_h6)

question: Which of the following best describes raw, unorganized facts without context?

options.A: Knowledge
options.B: Wisdom
options.C: Information
options.D: Data

explanation: Data represents the raw, isolated facts, such as a single vital sign measurement, before they are processed or given context. [learn more](GNS113_U1_T1#GNS113_U1_T1_h2)

question: Why is teaching self-monitoring skills so important for clients with chronic metabolic conditions?

options.A: It completely eliminates the need for any future doctor appointments.
options.B: It allows the patient to diagnose other people in their community.
options.C: It proves that nurses no longer need to assess hospital clients.
options.D: It empowers patients to catch small imbalances before they become emergencies.

explanation: Spot on! When patients know how to check themselves, they stay in control and can spot warning signs before things turn into an emergency. [learn more](GNS222_U2_T15#GNS222_U2_T15_h7)

question: Why do adolescent girls need more iron in their diet?

options.A: To increase their overall body fat percentage
options.B: To prevent the onset of juvenile diabetes
options.C: To support rapid thickening of tooth enamel
options.D: To replace iron lost during monthly menstruation

explanation: Teens growing up face new changes; adolescent girls need extra iron to make up for what is lost during monthly periods and keep anaemia away. [learn more](GNS227_U7_T012#GNS227_U7_T012_h5)

question: Why must care homes undergo regular government inspections?

options.A: To determine the weekly menu options for the dining hall
options.B: To collect annual property taxes directly from the facility owners
options.C: To ensure compliance with safety, sanitation, and quality standards
options.D: To recruit nursing students for government hospital positions

explanation: You nailed it! Regular checks make sure facilities keep up high standards of cleanliness, safety, and patient care. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T12#GNS324_U5_T12_h3)

question: What blood glucose level is generally used to define hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar) in clinical practice?

options.A: Above 11.1 mmol/L (200 mg/dL)
options.B: Below 6.0 mmol/L (108 mg/dL)
options.C: Below 3.9 mmol/L (70 mg/dL)
options.D: Above 7.8 mmol/L (140 mg/dL)

explanation: Spot on! Any reading under 3.9 mmol/L (70 mg/dL) means the blood sugar is too low and the patient needs help quickly. [learn more](GNS223_U7_T1#GNS223_U7_T1_h6)

question: Why is an efficient food distribution system vital for community health?

options.A: It ensures steady access to affordable and nourishing food
options.B: It guarantees that all crops are grown using organic methods
options.C: It stops farmers from selling their produce in local markets
options.D: It completely eliminates the need for agricultural subsidies

explanation: When distribution works well, communities receive a consistent supply of food, which prevents shortages and protects public nutrition. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T025#GNS227_U2_T025_h1)

question: A clinic pharmacy is running out of cash because staff members keep taking drugs on credit and rarely pay. What should management do?

options.A: Enforce a strict cash-and-carry policy for all individuals
options.B: Allow patients to take credit but exempt the hospital staff
options.C: Reduce the salaries of staff members who owe money for drugs
options.D: Increase the selling price of drugs to cover the unpaid credit

explanation: Strictly enforcing 'cash-and-carry' for everyone protects the fund. Allowing informal credit—even for staff—quickly drains the pharmacy's stock. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T3#GNS215_U3_T3_h7)

question: How is toxicology different from standard pharmacology?

options.A: Toxicology focuses specifically on harmful effects and poisons
options.B: Toxicology deals exclusively with the retail pricing of drugs
options.C: Toxicology only studies medications derived from synthetic chemicals
options.D: Toxicology examines how plant roots are crushed for remedies

explanation: Great job! While pharmacology studies all drug actions, toxicology zooms in strictly on poisons and harmful reactions. [learn more](GNS125_U1_T2#GNS125_U1_T2_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of a comprehensive pediatric assessment after a positive screening?

options.A: To establish a clear diagnosis and guide treatment planning
options.B: To replace the need for routine childhood immunizations
options.C: To prove that developmental delays are always temporary
options.D: To discharge the patient from the healthcare system permanently

explanation: A thorough assessment provides the specific medical and developmental diagnosis needed to build an effective care plan. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T6#GNS225_U5_T6_h3)

question: Why might people from different ethnic or genetic backgrounds process the same medication at different speeds?

options.A: The amount of water they drink hourly
options.B: How many meals they eat each day
options.C: Genetic variations in drug metabolism
options.D: The specific brand of pharmacy they use

explanation: Our genes naturally influence how liver enzymes break down drugs, meaning different people can process medications at different rates. Great to keep in mind for safe care! [learn more](GNS125_U3_T3#GNS125_U3_T3_h4)

question: What is the largest component of total daily energy expenditure for most people?

options.A: Planned athletic exercise
options.B: Basal or resting metabolic rate
options.C: Adaptive thermogenesis
options.D: Thermic effect of food

explanation: Keeping your internal organs alive and functioning at rest takes up the vast majority of the calories you burn daily. [learn more](GNS227_U4_T006#GNS227_U4_T006_h3)

question: What is the correct speed (rate) for giving breaths during neonatal positive pressure ventilation (PPV)?

options.A: 20 to 30 breaths per minute
options.B: 40 to 60 breaths per minute
options.C: 10 to 15 breaths per minute
options.D: 80 to 100 breaths per minute

explanation: When assisting a baby's breathing, aim for a steady, rhythmic pace of 40 to 60 breaths per minute to match a healthy newborn. [learn more](GNS226_U3_T010#GNS226_U3_T010_h4)

question: Who among the following is NOT usually in the high-risk group for severe food poisoning?

options.A: Healthy young adult office workers
options.B: Children under five years old
options.C: Older adults with chronic health conditions
options.D: Pregnant women and their babies

explanation: Exactly! Healthy young adults generally have strong immune systems to fight off food bugs easily. It's the very young, elderly, and pregnant women we worry about most. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T010#GNS227_U3_T010_h4)

question: Which hospital department usually conducts the financial check for an exemption request?

options.A: The main hospital kitchen
options.B: The hospital security department
options.C: The internal audit department
options.D: The social welfare unit

explanation: Social workers are specially trained to assess a patient's financial background and verify hardship before approving welfare waivers. [learn more](GNS215_U3_T6#GNS215_U3_T6_h6)

question: Why is picking the right research design so important for your everyday patient care?

options.A: It guarantees that every patient will recover quickly

options.C: It ensures findings are valid and useful for patient care
options.D: It eliminates the need for any statistical data analysis

explanation: You got it! A solid design cuts down errors so the evidence we find is safe and reliable enough to use right at the bedside. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T3#GNS224_U1_T3_h1)

question: A pregnant woman in a village clinic avoids meat and fish because elders said it causes difficult labor. What is the main health risk here?

options.A: Severe dehydration from high sodium intake
options.B: Maternal anemia and poor fetal development
options.C: Excessive weight gain during the first trimester
options.D: Sudden elevation of blood glucose levels

explanation: Skipping protein and iron during pregnancy denies both mother and baby essential building blocks, which can lead to anemia and slow growth. [learn more](GNS225_U6_T9#GNS225_U6_T9_h3)

question: What is the main difference between civil liability and criminal liability for a nurse?

options.A: Criminal liability is resolved through financial compensation to the patient.
options.B: Criminal liability addresses offenses against the state punishable by jail or fines.
options.C: Civil liability only applies to doctors, never to registered nurses.
options.D: Civil liability involves state imprisonment while criminal involves apologies.

explanation: Criminal law deals with public safety offences prosecuted by the state (like jail time or fines), whereas civil law is usually about private disputes and compensation. Good to know for practice! [learn more](GST321_U10_T4#GST321_U10_T4_h4)

question: Why is artificial airway displacement a major risk during ambulance transport?

options.A: Road vibration and vehicle movement can easily dislodge the tube
options.B: The driver's speed causes the patient's trachea to shorten
options.C: Patients intentionally pull their own breathing tubes out
options.D: Changes in altitude outside automatically push the tube deeper

explanation: Constant bouncing and transfers from stretcher to stretcher put mechanical stress on secured airways, requiring constant visual checks. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T9#GNS315_U3_T9_h3)

question: Which symptom suggests a patient's pain is from retained tissue rather than normal recovery?

options.A: Temporary loss of appetite for a few hours
options.B: Mild lower back ache that goes away with rest
options.C: Itchy skin rash on the arms and chest
options.D: Severe cramping accompanied by heavy bleeding or large clots

question: What is the absolute first priority for a nurse right after discovering a medication error has harmed a patient?

options.A: Assessing and stabilizing the patient's clinical condition
options.B: Notifying the nursing union representative immediately
options.C: Filling out the official hospital incident report form
options.D: Calling the legal department to secure representation

explanation: Patient safety and physical stabilization always come first before any paperwork or administrative duties are completed. [learn more](GST319_U6_T1#GST319_U6_T1_h3)

question: What triggers a tapeworm cyst to release its head (scolex) once a human eats contaminated meat?

options.A: Gastric acid and enzymes digesting the cyst wall to release the scolex
options.B: Immune system suppression caused by the larval waste products
options.C: The low temperature inside the human small intestine
options.D: Direct contact with human blood cells in the mucosal lining

explanation: Exactly! Stomach acid and digestive juices break open the cyst, freeing the scolex so it can attach firmly to the small intestine. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T24#GNS313_U2_T24_h2)

question: What is a common myth that scares young people away from hormonal contraception?

options.A: It automatically increases an individual's height by ten inches
options.B: It turns eye color into a completely different shade overnight
options.C: It causes permanent internal accumulation or organ rotting
options.D: It cures all forms of infectious diseases instantly

explanation: Baseless fears about pills piling up inside the body are common myths. Patient education clears this right up! [learn more](GNS312_U3_T10#GNS312_U3_T10_h7)

question: What should NOT be included in professional clinical notes after an emergency?

options.A: Exact timelines of all emergency interventions performed
options.B: Medication names, exact dosages, and administration times
options.C: The patient's physical response to the medical treatment
options.D: Personal opinions about the patient's family behavior

explanation: Keep notes strictly factual and professional. Leave out personal opinions or judgements about family members. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T12#GNS225_U3_T12_h9)

question: How can a clinic nurse best support a teenage girl looking for reproductive health advice?

options.A: Publicly reprimand her to discourage other teenagers
options.B: Report her immediately to local religious authorities
options.C: Provide confidential, non-judgmental counseling in a private space
options.D: Refuse service until her parents come to sign a consent form

explanation: Youth-friendly care is all about trust, privacy, and a warm attitude. Making teens feel safe encourages them to seek proper health guidance. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T005#GNS226_U6_T005_h6)

question: Which sign tells you a limb with a tight, wrapping (circumferential) burn is developing compartment syndrome?

options.A: Sudden appearance of localized skin blisters
options.B: Hyperactive bowel sounds and abdominal pain
options.C: Elevated core body temperature and chills
options.D: Loss of distal pulses and capillary refill

explanation: As a circumferential burn swells, it acts like a tourniquet, cutting off circulation inside. Losing pulse and slow refill means pressure is dangerously high! [learn more](GNS213_U5_T4#GNS213_U5_T4_h8)

question: A patient having a severe allergic reaction has wheezing, swollen lips, and crashing blood pressure. What medication is given first?

options.A: Intramuscular epinephrine
options.B: Oral diphenhydramine
options.C: Subcutaneous insulin
options.D: Intravenous paracetamol

explanation: Brilliant! Epinephrine is a lifesaver in anaphylaxis because it quickly opens up the airways and brings blood pressure back up. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T1#GNS221_U3_T1_h4)

question: What is the main focus of occupational therapy in subacute care?

options.A: Helping patients perform daily self-care tasks like dressing and bathing
options.B: Managing complex intravenous medications and wound dressings
options.C: Assessing nutritional intake and feeding tube placement needs
options.D: Restoring walking ability and lower body muscle strength

explanation: You nailed it! Occupational therapy focuses on helping clients get back to doing everyday activities independently. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T8#GNS324_U5_T8_h3)

question: Which serious complication involves kidney failure and red blood cell damage after certain bacterial infections?

options.A: Congestive heart failure
options.B: Acute respiratory distress
options.C: Diabetic ketoacidosis
options.D: Hemolytic uremic syndrome

explanation: Certain nasty bacterial toxins can attack tiny blood vessels, leading to a dangerous mix of kidney trouble, low platelets, and anemia. [learn more](GNS313_U2_T19#GNS313_U2_T19_h7)

question: Which of these actions is NOT allowed during a surgical hand scrub?

options.B: Leaning against the sink edge to rest your arms
options.C: Keeping your hands higher than your elbows
options.D: Standing at a safe distance from the sink

question: Why are recreational play breaks important alongside structured classroom lessons?

options.A: They allow teachers to grade papers without student interruptions
options.B: They provide a necessary mental break to refresh student focus
options.C: They ensure students never feel tired during school hours
options.D: They completely replace the need for physical education curricula

explanation: Brief periods of unstructured play reduce mental fatigue, helping students return to class more attentive and ready to learn. [learn more](GNS225_U4_T2#GNS225_U4_T2_h6)

question: What is the main goal of electrical cardioversion for a patient with a rapid, dangerous heart rhythm?

options.A: To permanently destroy the atrioventricular node
options.B: To reset the heart back to a normal sinus rhythm
options.C: To measure the exact cardiac output of the ventricles
options.D: To widen narrowed coronary arteries instantly

explanation: Cardioversion is like hitting 'restart' on a glitchy computer. It delivers a timed electrical shock to stop the chaos and let the heart's natural pacemaker take back control. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T3#GNS213_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why is it so important to encourage a patient to drink lots of fluids after a bone scan?

options.A: To prevent severe dehydration caused by the strong magnetic fields
options.B: To replace the fluid lost during the mandatory fasting period before the test
options.C: To activate the chemical tracer so it can take clearer pictures of the spine
options.D: To help flush the remaining radioactive tracer out of the body through urine

explanation: Drinking plenty of water helps the kidneys wash out any leftover radioactive tracer quickly, lowering radiation exposure. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T5#GNS222_U1_T5_h4)

question: What is the main goal of adding psychosocial support to post-abortion care?

options.A: To diagnose underlying psychiatric disorders through formal testing
options.B: To help patients process emotional distress, fear, and stigma
options.C: To convince patients to testify against unsafe abortion providers
options.D: To provide legal representation for women facing criminal charges

explanation: Spot on! Psychosocial support offers a safe, compassionate space to address the emotional trauma or guilt associated with pregnancy loss. [learn more](GNS226_U5_T021#GNS226_U5_T021_h5)

question: What is the main goal of using 'parallel forms reliability'?

options.A: To determine if survey questions relate to the same overall topic
options.B: To check if a single nurse can grade wounds consistently over days
options.C: To see if two different versions of a test yield equivalent results
options.D: To measure how much patients remember from their first clinic visit

explanation: Parallel forms just means Version A and Version B of a test match up equally well in measuring the same concept. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T27#GNS224_U1_T27_h6)

question: What is the main reason for placing a Word catheter after draining a Bartholin cyst?

options.A: To freeze and destroy the remaining cyst wall cells
options.B: To pump liquid antibiotics directly inside the cavity
options.C: To keep the new drainage opening open so a fresh duct can form
options.D: To permanently stop all fluid production in the body

explanation: The Word catheter has a tiny balloon at the tip and stays in for a few weeks. It keeps the wound open so it can heal into a permanent, normal drainage pathway. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T7#GNS216_U5_T7_h5)

question: Why are strict professional boundaries so important in home health care?

options.A: Patients living at home rarely build emotional connections
options.B: Home health agencies forbid nurses from talking to family members
options.C: The domestic setting makes personal and professional lines easy to blur
options.D: Nurses are legally considered family members while inside the house

explanation: Spot on! When you're sharing tea and chatting in a living room, it's easy to forget you're working. Keeping healthy boundaries keeps both you and the patient safe. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T10#GNS324_U1_T10_h4)

question: In the famous Swiss Cheese Model, what do the holes in the cheese slices represent?

options.A: Active weaknesses or gaps in safety defenses
options.B: Natural symptoms of a progressing illness
options.C: Successful steps in medication administration
options.D: Deliberate criminal acts committed by staff

explanation: Think of the holes as little gaps or weaknesses in our hospital safety checks that can occasionally let an error slip through. [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h4)

question: Why must rescue workers stabilize a victim before moving them to a hospital?

options.A: To address life-threatening injuries and prevent deterioration during transport
options.B: To ensure the rescue team gets enough rest before the next mission
options.C: To reduce the total paperwork required by the receiving hospital staff
options.D: To identify the personal belongings and insurance status of the patient

explanation: Brilliant! Stabilizing stops immediate threats like severe bleeding so the patient can survive the bumpy journey to the hospital. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T3#GNS315_U5_T3_h2)

question: What is the main advantage of running joint disaster drills with local and national agencies beforehand?

options.A: It guarantees that weather events will completely bypass the region
options.B: It removes all physical dangers associated with frontline rescue work
options.C: Familiarity with command structures helps eliminate bureaucratic delays during a real emergency
options.D: It reduces the financial cost of purchasing medical equipment

explanation: Practicing together builds teamwork and trust, so everyone coordinates smoothly when every second counts. [learn more](GNS315_U5_T1#GNS315_U5_T1_h6)

question: Why do we track a child's growth over several visits rather than relying on just one measurement?

options.A: It prevents errors made by community health volunteers
options.B: It shows the direction and velocity of growth over time
options.C: It guarantees the child will not contract infectious diseases
options.D: It is required by government health insurance policies

explanation: A single visit only tells you about today. Tracking over time shows the true pattern—whether the child is growing well or falling behind. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T55#GNS214_U1_T55_h1)

question: Which food should a nurse advise a patient with very weak immunity to avoid?

options.A: Thoroughly boiled white rice
options.B: Cooked skinless chicken breast
options.C: Peeled and cooked carrots
options.D: Unpasteurized fresh milk

question: Which patients do standard precautions apply to in the hospital?

options.A: Only patients who have open wounds

question: Why do nurses need to understand the basics of where our food comes from?

options.A: Many chronic health issues and nutritional deficiencies originate in the food system

options.C: Hospital kitchens are managed directly by nursing staff

question: Why is health care waste management so important in our hospitals?

question: What is the main job of the tiny balloon cuff on an endotracheal tube?

options.C: To measure the patient's blood pressure
options.D: To secure the tube in place and prevent aspiration

question: Which lifestyle habit helps improve blood vessel health for men dealing with sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Regular physical exercise and weight loss
options.B: Increasing daily caffeine consumption
options.C: Reducing total hours of sleep each night
options.D: Avoiding all forms of dietary carbohydrates

question: What is the main difference between constructive and destructive conflict in a healthcare team?

options.A: Constructive conflict only happens in hospitals, while destructive conflict happens in clinics

options.C: Constructive conflict improves patient care ideas, while destructive conflict harms team morale

question: Which type of germ is usually behind a sudden outbreak of waterborne stomach illness?

question: As a community health nurse, you notice several villagers showing signs of fever and yellow eyes. What is your best immediate action?

options.B: Distribute mosquito repellent creams without informing the government

question: Why do nurses flush an intermittent IV line with normal saline right after giving a medication?

question: What is the very first thing a health worker must do during community entry?

question: In a busy clinical ward, what do we mean by 'alarm fatigue'?

options.C: Physical exhaustion caused by carrying mobile alert devices

question: How do nurses determine if a specific disease rate in a community is a serious problem?

question: When assigning nursing duties on a shift, what should guide you besides just counting patients?

question: What is the best position to place a patient in before you start feeding them?

question: A patient has swollen ankles. How should you advise them to position their legs when resting?

options.C: Flat on the floor while sitting in a chair

question: When is the risk of maternal and newborn complications highest after delivery?

options.A: After the sixth month
options.B: Within the first 48 hours

question: Which way of spreading germs involves tiny particles floating in the air over long distances?

question: What is a major dual benefit of school feeding programs?

options.B: Improving child nutrition and boosting school attendance
options.C: Training children to become professional commercial farmers
options.D: Eliminating the need for children to ever visit a doctor

explanation: School meals fight hunger while giving families an extra incentive to keep children in school. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T028#GNS227_U2_T028_h6)

question: According to Herzberg, which of the following is considered a hygiene factor?

options.D: Public recognition for an outstanding award

explanation: Hygiene factors prevent job dissatisfaction and include basic needs like fair pay, safe environment, and job security. [learn more](GST321_U1_T13#GST321_U1_T13_h5)

question: A community nurse is planning a flood drill for a neighborhood with many toddlers. What is the most important factor to keep in mind?

options.B: They know how to operate community emergency radios

question: What does the social ecology framework primarily examine when studying adolescent health?

options.B: The entire surrounding environment and social network of the teenager
options.C: The specific biological changes happening during puberty
options.D: The financial status of the local healthcare facility

explanation: Social ecology looks at how multiple layers of a person's social environment interact to influence their overall health and behavior. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T20#GNS312_U3_T20_h1)

question: Why is applied research so helpful in everyday clinical nursing?

options.A: It relies entirely on mathematical formulas instead of patients
options.B: It aims to solve immediate, practical patient care problems
options.C: It never requires ethical approval from an institutional board
options.D: It costs nothing to conduct in a busy hospital ward

explanation: You nailed it! Applied research tackles the real, everyday challenges we face right there at the bedside. [learn more](GNS217_U1_T1#GNS217_U1_T1_h5)

question: An immunization campaign targets 500 children, and each child requires 3 doses. Using a 10% waste factor, how many total syringes are needed?

question: Which seasonal weather condition in northern Nigeria is famous for triggering outbreaks of cerebrospinal meningitis?

options.A: The dry harmattan season
options.B: The cold December nights
options.C: The heavy rainy season
options.D: The coastal flooding period

explanation: Well done! The dry harmattan brings dust and low humidity that irritate our airways, making meningitis outbreaks more common during this time. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T89#GNS214_U1_T89_h3)

question: In community health nursing, who is considered the primary 'client'?

options.A: Only the children under five years old
options.B: The local government chairman
options.C: The medical director of the district hospital
options.D: The entire population of the community

question: Why is it important to involve local community assets during resource mobilization?

options.A: Government policy forbids spending money on outside contractors
options.B: Local villagers are the only people legally allowed to handle medical drugs
options.C: It eliminates the need for nurses to write any project reports
options.D: It builds local ownership and reduces complete reliance on external funding

explanation: Using local resources ensures the community values the project and can sustain it even if external donors leave. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T15#GNS225_U2_T15_h5)

question: Why must you wait for the skin antiseptic to dry completely before inserting the needle?

options.A: To make the skin tougher so the needle enters smoothly
options.B: To ensure the tourniquet stays firmly in place on the skin
options.C: To prevent the adhesive bandage from sticking too early
options.D: To allow the chemical to kill microorganisms and prevent sample damage

explanation: Patience is key! Giving the antiseptic time to dry lets it kill germs properly and stops wet alcohol from stinging the patient or ruining the blood sample. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T8#GNS122_U1_T8_h5)

question: Why is catching a high-risk pregnancy early so important for us as nurses?

options.A: It guarantees that the baby will be born without any congenital defects
options.B: It completely stops the mother from experiencing any physical discomfort
options.C: It allows the healthcare team to plan timely interventions and prevent complications
options.D: It removes the need for any laboratory tests during the third trimester

explanation: Spotting risks early gives you and the medical team time to step in and manage things smoothly before they become emergency situations. Great nursing instinct! [learn more](GNS226_U2_T010#GNS226_U2_T010_h1)

question: Why is watching a patient actually do a household task better than just asking if they can do it?

options.A: Patients often lie to nurses to avoid being sent away to a hospital.
options.B: Verbal reports may not match the patient's actual physical capability.
options.C: Patients forget the names of the tools they use for cooking and cleaning.
options.D: Direct observation is a mandatory legal requirement in all provinces.

explanation: Spot on! People often overestimate what they can do or try to hide their struggles, so watching them yourself gives you the true picture. [learn more](GNS324_U3_T6#GNS324_U3_T6_h4)

question: What is the main goal of leadership in nursing?

options.A: Handling financial budgets and payroll duties
options.B: Completing individual patient tasks in isolation
options.C: Enforcing strict hospital rules without questioning
options.D: Guiding and inspiring others to achieve common goals

explanation: Great job! Leadership is all about bringing people together and motivating your team to reach shared healthcare goals. [learn more](GST321_U3_T1#GST321_U3_T1_h1)

question: What is the primary operational feature of a day care centre?

options.B: Care is provided exclusively during severe medical emergencies
options.C: Children stay overnight throughout the entire week
options.D: Clients return home to their families every evening

question: What is the main goal of using radiation therapy in cancer treatment?

options.A: Cleansing the entire circulatory system of loose circulating tumor cells

question: What is a standard admission rule for most half-way houses?

question: Under standard precautions, when should a nurse wear gloves?

question: How can the government best tackle the problem of nurses refusing postings to remote rural clinics due to poor living conditions?

question: Which action best reflects a comprehensive psychiatric nursing assessment?

question: A stroke survivor struggles to button their shirt and prepare meals independently. Which therapist is best suited to address these challenges?

question: Why do clinics use the WHO staging system for HIV when lab tests for CD4 count are missing?

explanation: Correct! HIV specifically targets CD4+ T-cells, using them to make copies of itself and gradually weakening the body's immune defense. [learn more](GNS312_U3_T15#GNS312_U3_T15_h4)

question: What happens if the body fails to maintain proper immune tolerance?

options.A: Innate barriers permanently lose their ability to secrete mucus
options.B: Primary lymphoid organs immediately stop producing white blood cells
options.C: The immune system attacks the body's own healthy cells and tissues
options.D: The body becomes completely defenseless against minor viral colds

explanation: Correct! When tolerance fails, the body stops recognizing 'self' and starts an autoimmune attack on its own healthy organs. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T1#GNS123_U4_T1_h7)

question: A nurse and a social worker disagree on how to discharge an elderly patient who lives alone. What should guide their next step?

options.A: Following the nurse's plan because nurses spend more time at the bedside
options.B: Letting the patient leave without any support services
options.C: Focusing on the patient's needs through shared decision-making
options.D: Escalating the disagreement to the hospital director immediately

explanation: Exactly! When team members see things differently, putting the patient's welfare first and talking it through always points the way forward. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T24#GNS225_U2_T24_h2)

question: What is a simple, cheap way villagers can stop themselves from swallowing Guinea worm larvae in their drinking water?

options.A: Adding tablespoons of cooking oil to the water
options.B: Exposing the water bucket to direct moonlight
options.C: Stirring the water vigorously with a wooden spoon
options.D: Filtering water through a clean cloth

explanation: You got it! A simple cloth filter catches the tiny fleas carrying the larvae. Public health nursing is often about simple, effective tools! [learn more](GNS313_U2_T23#GNS313_U2_T23_h8)

question: A client with a terminal degenerative disorder can still speak clearly. When should you discuss advance directives and end-of-life wishes with them?

options.A: While the client is still capable of making and expressing their own decisions
options.B: Never, because family members should make all healthcare choices
options.C: Only after the client loses consciousness in the final hours of life
options.D: During the initial diagnostic blood test before the disease is explained

explanation: It is best to discuss advance directives early while the client is still of sound mind to ensure their personal wishes are truly honored. [learn more](GNS222_U4_T15#GNS222_U4_T15_h8)

question: Which natural hazard displaces thousands of people every year in Nigerian coastal and river areas?

options.A: Tidal tsunamis
options.B: Seasonal flooding
options.C: Volcanic eruptions
options.D: Severe blizzards

explanation: Exactly! Heavy seasonal rains often overflow river banks, causing widespread displacement in many parts of Nigeria. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T12#GNS315_U1_T12_h2)

question: A ward manager wants to speed up patient discharges. Using systems thinking, what is the best first step?

options.A: Examine how nursing, pharmacy, and transport work together during discharge
options.B: Force the nursing staff to work faster without talking to others
options.C: Focus only on speeding up the discharge lounge staff
options.D: Punish nurses whose patients take too long to leave

explanation: To fix a delay, you have to look at the whole chain of events, not just one group of workers. [learn more](GST319_U2_T3#GST319_U2_T3_h2)

question: What is the main difference between incidence and prevalence?

options.A: Incidence is used for chronic diseases, while prevalence is for injuries
options.B: Incidence counts only new cases, while prevalence counts all existing cases
options.C: Incidence measures past history, while prevalence predicts future risk
options.D: Incidence requires a blood test, while prevalence is calculated by survey

explanation: Incidence tracks newly developing cases, whereas prevalence tracks the total burden of existing cases. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h5)

question: Why are modern hospitals moving away from just blaming individuals when mistakes happen?

options.A: Because fixing underlying system flaws prevents future errors better
options.B: Because hospital management no longer cares about errors
options.C: Because nurses refuse to complete incident reports
options.D: Because punishing workers stops all future mistakes

explanation: Looking at system problems instead of just pointing fingers helps fix the root cause so the same mistake doesn't happen again. Great nursing practice starts with understanding this! [learn more](GST319_U5_T5#GST319_U5_T5_h1)

question: What is the main purpose of running biochemical tests on an isolated microbe?

options.A: To see what chemical reactions and nutrients the microbe uses, helping identify the species
options.B: To make the bacteria glow brightly under ordinary room lighting
options.C: To measure how fast liquid broth evaporates in a warm room
options.D: To completely destroy the cell wall so the organism dissolves

explanation: Well done! Biochemical tests check how a germ processes different chemicals, giving scientists a clear chemical fingerprint to identify it. [learn more](GST114_U5_T2#GST114_U5_T2_h6)

question: Which international declaration in 1978 made Primary Health Care the main strategy for global health?

options.A: The Alma-Ata Declaration
options.B: The Geneva Nursing Charter
options.C: The Lagos Health Accord
options.D: The London Sanitary Treaty

explanation: Remember Alma-Ata! The 1978 conference put Primary Health Care on the map as the key to health for everyone. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T6#GNS225_U2_T6_h5)

question: Which anti-TB drug requires regular checks on a patient's vision and color sight?

options.A: Pyrazinamide
options.B: Isoniazid
options.C: Rifampin
options.D: Ethambutol

explanation: Ethambutol can affect eye health (optic neuritis). Regular eye checks help catch any vision changes early before they become serious. [learn more](GNS324_U4_T18#GNS324_U4_T18_h8)
